html:
Cyclone Gonu was a tropical cyclone that struck the coast of Oman in June 2007, the strongest storm then recorded in the Arabian Sea.

It weakened before landfall but brought torrential rain to a dry country. Floods tore through the dry valleys, or wadis, of Muscat and the east coast, killing dozens of people, cutting water and power, and damaging roads and homes. It then crossed to Iran.

Gonu was the worst natural disaster in modern Oman. It showed how exposed the fast-growing cities of the Gulf coast are to storms from the Indian Ocean. Oman was hit again by Cyclone Phet in 2010 and Shaheen in 2021. Compare the modern state that had to answer it.
sum: Cyclone Gonu was a tropical cyclone that struck the coast of Oman in June 2007, the strongest storm then recorded in the Arabian Sea.
